items.title: Finite-budget nonlinear FAS two-grid cycle
items.statement:
Let $U_h\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_h}$ and $U_H\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_H}$ be open,
with $n_h,n_H\ge1$. Let $F_h:U_h\to\mathbb R^{n_h}$ and
$F_H:U_H\to\mathbb R^{n_H}$ be residual maps, and let $f_h\in\mathbb R^{n_h}$.
The equation on the fine level is $F_h(u)=f_h$. Choose linear maps
$I: \mathbb R^{n_h}\to\mathbb R^{n_H}$ (iterate restriction),
$R: \mathbb R^{n_h}\to\mathbb R^{n_H}$ (residual restriction), and
$P: \mathbb R^{n_H}\to\mathbb R^{n_h}$ (prolongation). No equality among
$I$, $R$, and $P$ is imposed by this definition. Choose positive diagonal
matrices $D^{\rm pre}$ and $D^{\rm post}$, damping factors
$0<\omega_{\rm pre},\omega_{\rm post}\le1$, finite sweep counts
$\nu_{\rm pre},\nu_{\rm post}\in\mathbb N_0$, a finite positive coarse-solver
operation budget $B_H$, and a positive integer $\gamma$.

A **coarse-solver call** with target $g\in\mathbb R^{n_H}$ and initial value
$z\in U_H$ must return within $B_H$ declared operations either an exact selected
root $(v,\texttt{exact-root},0)$ with $F_H(v)=g$, an inexact value
$(v,\texttt{inexact-root},\eta)$ with the explicitly computed residual
$\eta=\|F_H(v)-g\|_2>0$, or one of
$\texttt{branch-failure}$, $\texttt{domain-failure}$, and
$\texttt{budget-exhausted}$. The solver contract requires it to return the
initial value unchanged as `exact-root` when $F_H(z)=g$ and $z$ is the selected
root. A direct formula, an exact local branch, or a finite iterative solver may
be supplied; the definition makes no claim that any solver finds a root from an
arbitrary initial value.

For a starting fine iterate $u\in U_h$, do the following in exact real
arithmetic.

1. Perform $\nu_{\rm pre}$ nonlinear damped-Jacobi sweeps. In each sweep,
form the trial value
$$\widetilde u:=u-\omega_{\rm pre}(D^{\rm pre})^{-1}(F_h(u)-f_h).$$
If $\widetilde u\notin U_h$, return the current valid fine iterate $u$ with
status `domain-failure`; otherwise set $u:=\widetilde u$.

2. Set $u_H=Iu$. If $u_H\notin U_H$, return the last valid fine iterate
with status `domain-failure`. Otherwise set $r_h=f_h-F_h(u)$ and
$$g_H=F_H(u_H)+Rr_h=Rf_h+\tau(u),\qquad \tau(u):=F_H(Iu)-RF_h(u).$$

3. Set $z=u_H$ and initialize a finite diagnostic list $\Delta=()$. For
$t=1,\ldots,\gamma$, call the declared coarse solver on $(g_H,z,B_H)$. On
`branch-failure`, `domain-failure`, or `budget-exhausted`, return the last
valid fine iterate with that status and the diagnostics accumulated so far.
On `exact-root` or `inexact-root`, append the returned status and residual to
$\Delta$, replace $z$ by the returned value, and append any nested diagnostics
returned by the coarse call. Reusing $g_H$ while starting at the current $z$
makes repeated coarse calls a bounded V/W-style cycle.

4. Form the trial correction
$$\widetilde u:=u+P(z-Iu).$$
If $\widetilde u\notin U_h$, return the current valid fine iterate $u$ with
status `domain-failure` and $\Delta$; otherwise set $u:=\widetilde u$.

5. Perform $\nu_{\rm post}$ nonlinear damped-Jacobi sweeps. In each sweep,
form the trial value
$$\widetilde u:=u-\omega_{\rm post}(D^{\rm post})^{-1}(F_h(u)-f_h).$$
If $\widetilde u\notin U_h$, return the current valid fine iterate $u$ with
status `domain-failure` and $\Delta$; otherwise set $u:=\widetilde u$.
Compute the final fine residual
$\eta_h:=\|F_h(u)-f_h\|_2$. Return the resulting iterate with status
`exact-root` and residual $0$ if $\eta_h=0$, and with status `inexact-root`
and residual $\eta_h$ if $\eta_h>0$, together with $\Delta$. Thus the status
used when this procedure is called recursively
always certifies the residual for its own level equation; zero residuals
reported by inner coarse calls do not by themselves certify that the returned
fine iterate is a root.

Every loop count and solver budget is finite. `V` and `W` refer to the cases
$\gamma=1$ and $\gamma=2$. A multi-level cycle uses this two-grid procedure at
each level, with the next-level cycle supplied as the coarse solver and a
finite level cap. Fixed-point consistency, linear reduction, local convergence,
and work bounds are separate claims.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6
Harald van Brummelen, Basics of Multigrid Methods, SINTEF winter-school lecture notes
Van Emden Henson, Multigrid Methods for Nonlinear Problems: An Overview, UCRL-JC-150259

items.title: Second derivative formula for a composed cycle map
items.statement:
Let $X_0,X_1,X_2,X_3$ be finite-dimensional real Euclidean spaces and let
$U_i\subseteq X_i$ be open for $i=0,1,2$. Suppose $S:U_0\to U_1$, $C:U_1\to U_2$, and
$T:U_2\to X_3$ are $C^2$, meaning that each is totally differentiable with
continuous derivative and that its derivative map is itself totally
differentiable. Write $\mathcal L(X,Y)$ for the finite-dimensional space of
linear maps $X\to Y$ with the induced Euclidean operator norm. Put
$E=T\circ C\circ S$. For a $C^2$ map $f$, define
$D^2f(x)[h,k]:=(D(Df)(x)h)k$. At $x\in U_0$, set $y=S(x)$ and
$z=C(y)$. Then for all $h,k\in X_0$,
$$D^2E(x)[h,k]=D^2T(z)[DC(y)DS(x)h,DC(y)DS(x)k]+DT(z)\bigl(D^2C(y)[DS(x)h,DS(x)k]+DC(y)D^2S(x)[h,k]\bigr).$$
items.strategy: Differentiate the first-derivative composition identity using the bounded bilinear product rule, then apply the result twice.

references.title: Chin-Lung Wang, Banach Calculus, §§2.1.1–2.1.4 and §2.3

items.title: Finite-budget recursive nonlinear FAS V/W cycle
items.statement:
Fix a finite hierarchy of levels $j=0,1,\ldots,J$ with $J\ge1$. At level
$j$, let $F_j:U_j\to\mathbb R^{n_j}$ be defined on an open
$U_j\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_j}$, let $f_j\in\mathbb R^{n_j}$, and provide the
linear transfers $I_j$, $R_j$, and $P_j$ with the dimensions in
[[alg-fas-two-grid-cycle]]. For each $j>0$, provide the two diagonal smoother
matrices, damping factors, and finite pre/post sweep counts from that
algorithm. Choose a finite base solver at level $0$ with a declared total
operation budget $B_0$ and statuses `exact-root`, `inexact-root`, `branch-failure`,
`domain-failure`, and `budget-exhausted`. Its `exact-root` and `inexact-root`
statuses must report $\|F_0(v)-f_0\|_2$ as $0$ and a positive number,
respectively. At each noncoarsest level choose
$\gamma_j\in\{1,2\}$, representing V and W recursion, respectively.
For every $j>0$, the recursive level-$(j-1)$ solver call in the two-grid
procedure is metered against its declared finite coarse-call budget; if it
exceeds that budget, it returns `budget-exhausted` with its last valid iterate.

The base-solver contract also requires it to return its initial value unchanged
with status `exact-root` whenever that value already satisfies $F_0(z)=f_0$.

Define $\operatorname{Cycle}(0,u,f_0)$ to call the base solver. For $j>0$,
provide the level-$(j-1)$ cycle as the coarse-solver interface to
[[alg-fas-two-grid-cycle]]: its reported residual is measured as
$\|F_{j-1}(v)-g\|_2$, where $v$ is the returned value, with `exact-root` only
at residual zero and `inexact-root`
only at positive residual. The two-grid procedure makes $\gamma_j$ calls
with the same coarse right side $g$ and the current coarse iterate $z$.
Return the two-grid output, its status, its level residual, and the finite
diagnostic list of coarse-call residuals. Any failure status propagates
immediately with the last valid fine-level iterate. Each recursive call
lowers $j$, and all within-level loops have the finite budgets required by
[[alg-fas-two-grid-cycle]].

The V-cycle is the choice $\gamma_j=1$ on each noncoarsest level; the W-cycle
is $\gamma_j=2$. This definition does not assert that the returned iterate
solves the nonlinear equations, that the cycles converge, or that their work
is linear in the number of fine unknowns.

items.title: Derivative of the exact-branch FAS two-grid cycle
items.statement:
Consider one exact-branch two-grid cycle from [[alg-fas-two-grid-cycle]]. Let
$F_h:U_h\to\mathbb R^{n_h}$ and $F_H:U_H\to\mathbb R^{n_H}$ be $C^1$ on
open sets, let $I,R,P$ be linear, and suppose $F_h(u_*)=f_h$ and
$Iu_*\in U_H$. Assume the exact coarse solver selects the local root branch
through $Iu_*$ and $DF_H(Iu_*)$ is invertible. Suppose the pre/post smoothing
maps are $C^1$ and fix $u_*$. The selected coarse root $v(u)$ is locally $C^1$,
and the derivative of the actual FAS cycle $E$ at $u_*$ is
$$DE(u_*)=DS^{\rm post}(u_*)\bigl[I_{n_h}-P\,DF_H(Iu_*)^{-1}R\,DF_h(u_*)\bigr]DS^{\rm pre}(u_*).$$

No identity between $R$ and $I$, or between the coarse operator and a
rediscretized fine operator, is assumed in this derivative formula.
items.strategy: Differentiate the coarse equation by the Euclidean implicit function theorem, then apply the chain rule to the correction and both smoothers.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6
Harald van Brummelen, Basics of Multigrid Methods, SINTEF winter-school lecture notes

items.title: A finite FAS V/W cycle terminates with bounded stated work
items.statement:
Consider an invocation of [[alg-fas-vw-cycle]] on levels $0,\ldots,J$, where
the base solver uses at most $B_0<\infty$ counted operations, every nonlinear
smoother update and residual evaluation returns in finite work, and every
transfer and correction is a finite-dimensional map evaluation. The
invocation terminates with one of its declared statuses. If $W_j$ is the
maximum counted work of a level-$j$ invocation, then
$$W_0\le B_0,\qquad W_j\le C_j+\gamma_jW_{j-1}\quad(1\le j\le J),$$
where $C_j$ is the finite work of that level's pre-smoothing, residual and
transfer evaluations, correction, post-smoothing, and status/diagnostic
bookkeeping. This recurrence counts the actual nonlinear smoother,
coarse-solve, and returned-diagnostic work; it implies no blanket $O(n_J)$
estimate.
items.strategy: Induct on the level and count each bounded smoother, recursive call, transfer, correction, and base-solver operation.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6
Harald van Brummelen, Basics of Multigrid Methods, SINTEF winter-school lecture notes

items.title: An exact fine root is fixed by the FAS V/W cycle
items.statement:
For a level-$j$ invocation of [[alg-fas-vw-cycle]], let $u^*$ satisfy
$F_j(u^*)=f_j$. Suppose each selected pre/post smoother leaves every exact
root fixed, every restriction $I_ju^*$ lies in $U_{j-1}$ and is selected as
the exact coarse root at its zero-defect target, and the base solver returns
any initial exact root unchanged. Then the exact-branch FAS V/W cycle leaves
$u^*$ fixed. This holds for arbitrary admissible transfer maps $I_j,R_j,P_j$;
no identity such as $R_j=I_j$ or $I_jP_j=I$ is needed.
items.strategy: Induct over the hierarchy and substitute the exact fine root into each tau-corrected coarse equation.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6
Harald van Brummelen, Basics of Multigrid Methods, SINTEF winter-school lecture notes
Van Emden Henson, Multigrid Methods for Nonlinear Problems: An Overview, UCRL-JC-150259

items.title: A smooth FAS cycle converges locally under its actual derivative bounds
items.statement:
Let $E:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be the actual exact-branch error map of one fixed
FAS two-grid or recursive V/W cycle, with $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ open. Let
$u_*\in U$ be a fine root for which the selected smoothers and coarse branches
fix $u_*$, so $E(u_*)=u_*$. Assume $E$ is $C^1$ on a neighborhood of the
closed Euclidean ball $K=\overline B_2(u_*,r)\subset U$. Put
$q=\|DE(u_*)\|_{\rm op}$, where for a linear map $T$ the induced Euclidean
operator norm is $\|T\|_{\rm op}:=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|Tv\|_2$. Suppose $q<1$ and
$$\|DE(x)-DE(y)\|_{\rm op}\le L\|x-y\|_2\qquad(x,y\in K)$$
for some $L\ge0$. If $q+Lr/2<1$, then $E(K)\subseteq K$ and every iteration
$u_{k+1}=E(u_k)$ starting in $K$ satisfies
$$\|u_k-u_*\|_2\le(q+Lr/2)^k\|u_0-u_*\|_2.$$
This is a local result for the derivative of the actual cycle; it supplies no
global-start or mesh-independent rate unless $q,L,r$ are verified uniformly.
items.strategy: Apply the mean-value integral formula to E and bound the derivative variation by L times the distance from the root.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6

items.title: A linear Galerkin V/W cycle is translation-covariant
items.statement:
For the linear Galerkin V/W-cycle procedure of [[alg-finite-galerkin-v-cycle]],
on any level $j$ and for all $x,a,b\in\mathbb R^{n_j}$,
$$\operatorname{Cycle}(j,x+a,b+A_ja)=a+\operatorname{Cycle}(j,x,b).$$
The identity is in exact arithmetic and uses the same hierarchy, smoothing
matrices, sweep counts, and cycle count on both sides.
items.strategy: Compare the two runs level by level, using invariant residuals and identical deterministic coarse-error inputs.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6
Harald van Brummelen, Basics of Multigrid Methods, SINTEF winter-school lecture notes
Van Emden Henson, Multigrid Methods for Nonlinear Problems: An Overview, UCRL-JC-150259

items.title: Linear FAS exactly reduces to a Galerkin correction V/W cycle
items.statement:
Let $A_j\in\mathbb R^{n_j\times n_j}$, $0\le j\le J$, be a finite SPD
Galerkin hierarchy with full-column-rank prolongations $P_j$ and
$A_{j-1}=P_j^{\mathsf T}A_jP_j$. At each level set $F_j(u)=A_ju$,
$R_j=P_j^{\mathsf T}$, and use the exact Galerkin coarse operator
$F_{j-1}(v)=A_{j-1}v$, matching residual-correction pre/post smoothers, and
the same finite sweep and V/W cycle counts in [[alg-fas-vw-cycle]] and
[[alg-finite-galerkin-v-cycle]]. The exact-branch FAS V/W procedure returns
exactly the same iterate as the corresponding linear Galerkin correction
V/W-cycle. The iterate restriction $I_j$ may be any linear map of the stated
dimensions.
items.strategy: Induct on levels, subtract A_H Iu from the tau-corrected coarse equation, and identify the resulting coarse residual-correction equation.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6
Harald van Brummelen, Basics of Multigrid Methods, SINTEF winter-school lecture notes
Van Emden Henson, Multigrid Methods for Nonlinear Problems: An Overview, UCRL-JC-150259

items.title: An inexact FAS coarse solve contributes a bounded correction defect
items.statement:
Consider one two-grid FAS cycle with fixed pre-smoothing result, exact selected
coarse root $v(u)$, prolongation $P$, and a post-smoother that is
$L_{\rm post}$-Lipschitz on the relevant corrected states. Suppose a coarse
solver returns $\widehat v$ with residual
$\eta=\|F_H(\widehat v)-g_H(u)\|_2$ and a separately verified
residual-to-solution estimate
$$\|\widehat v-v(u)\|_2\le M_H\eta.$$
Then the inexact-cycle output $\widehat E(u)$ and exact-cycle output $E(u)$
satisfy
$$\|\widehat E(u)-E(u)\|_2\le L_{\rm post}\|P\|_{\rm op}M_H\eta.$$
If the exact cycle satisfies the root-error estimate
$\|E(u)-u_*\|_2\le\kappa\|u-u_*\|_2$ on a stated invariant region, then
for every iteration input $u_k$ in that region whose exact and inexact
corrected states satisfy the preceding hypotheses,
$$\|u_{k+1}-u_*\|_2\le\kappa\|u_k-u_*\|_2+L_{\rm post}\|P\|_{\rm op}M_H\eta_k.$$
Invertibility of $DF_H$ alone is not asserted to imply the stated
residual-to-solution estimate; that bound must be proved under additional
coarse-operator hypotheses.
items.strategy: Subtract the exact and inexact coarse corrections and apply the declared residual-to-solution bound and prolongation norm.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6
Harald van Brummelen, Basics of Multigrid Methods, SINTEF winter-school lecture notes
Van Emden Henson, Multigrid Methods for Nonlinear Problems: An Overview, UCRL-JC-150259

items.title: A two-node semilinear diffusion FAS cycle has an explicit local rate
items.statement:
On $\Omega=(0,3)$ with homogeneous endpoint values, the $h=1$ centered
finite-difference discretization of the semilinear equation
$-u''+u^3=0$ has fine residual
$$F(u)=Au+(u_1^3,u_2^3),\qquad A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}.$$
Use $P=(1,1)^{\mathsf T}$, $Iu=(u_1+u_2)/2$, $R=P^{\mathsf T}$, the
Galerkin coarse residual $F_H(v)=P^{\mathsf T}F(Pv)$, one pre- and one
post-sweep $S(u)=u-\tfrac14F(u)$, and the exact selected coarse root. The
unique fine root is $u_*=0$. The actual exact-branch FAS two-grid map is a
contraction toward $u_*$ on $\overline B_2(0,1/100)$ with error factor at most
$27/400$.
items.strategy: Compute the strong monotonicity, exact coarse branch, cycle derivative, and a uniform second-derivative bound on the stated ball.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6
Harald van Brummelen, Basics of Multigrid Methods, SINTEF winter-school lecture notes
Van Emden Henson, Multigrid Methods for Nonlinear Problems: An Overview, UCRL-JC-150259

items.title: The tau term recovers the restricted root in reaction Poisson
items.statement:
For the finite-difference semilinear reaction operator
$F_h(u)=Au+(u_1^3,u_2^3)$ with
$A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$, take
$P=(1,1)^{\mathsf T}$, $Iu=(u_1+u_2)/2$, $R=P^{\mathsf T}$, and the Galerkin
coarse operator $F_H(v)=P^{\mathsf T}F_h(Pv)=2v+2v^3$. For the manufactured
fine root $u_*=(1,0)$ and $f_h=F_h(u_*)$, the tau correction is $-3/4$ and
the exact coarse branch returns $Iu_*=1/2$, so the corrected fine iterate is
still $u_*$.
items.strategy: Substitute the manufactured fine root into the fine residual, restricted residual, coarse operator, and tau expression.

items.title: Omitting tau can move an exact fine root
items.statement:
The claim that replacing the tau-corrected coarse right side by the restricted
fine right side $Rf_h$ always preserves an exact fine-grid root is false.
items.strategy: Use an SPD two-node fine matrix and a rediscretized coarse scalar operator that differs from its Galerkin value, then compute the no-tau coarse correction exactly.

items.title: The certified FAS contraction radius shrinks at a pitchfork
items.statement:
For $F_\mu(x,y)=(\mu x+x^3,y)$ with zero right side, use the coarse space
spanned by $(0,1)^{\mathsf T}$, iterate and residual restriction
$I(x,y)=R(x,y)=y$, coarse residual $F_H(v)=v$, and one pre- and one
post-sweep $S_\mu(x,y)=(x-\tfrac12(\mu x+x^3),y/2)$. The exact-branch FAS
cycle has root $(0,0)$ and derivative norm
$$q_\mu=(1-\mu/2)^2\qquad(0<\mu\le1).$$
For each such $\mu$, the local theorem certifies radius
$r_\mu=\sqrt{\mu/100}$, which tends to zero as the pitchfork parameter
approaches $0$.
items.strategy: Compute the coarse correction and the scalar smoother composition, then evaluate its derivative at the root.

items.title: A one-level linear FAS correction is the Galerkin correction
items.statement:
Take $A=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$,
$P=(1,1)^{\mathsf T}$, $Iu=(u_1+u_2)/2$, $R=P^{\mathsf T}$, and the Galerkin
coarse matrix $A_H=P^{\mathsf T}AP=2$. For any fine iterate $u$ and right
side $f$, the coarse FAS difference $v-Iu$ is exactly
$A_H^{-1}R(f-Au)$, and the prolongated update is the ordinary Galerkin
coarse correction.
items.strategy: Compute the coarse residual difference and compare it with the linear correction formula.
